items.def: to deal openly with worries that someone has raised
items.ex: We would like to address concerns about data security before we go any further.
items.why: Bedenken „ausräumen“ oder darauf „eingehen“ heißt address concerns, nicht solve concerns.

items.def: to tell others that you are worried about something
items.ex: If anyone wants to raise concerns about the timeline, please do it before Friday.
items.why: Bedenken „äußern“ heißt raise concerns, nicht say concerns.

items.def: to find a fair compromise between two things that pull in different directions
items.ex: We need to strike a balance between speed and compliance.
items.why: Einen Mittelweg „finden“ heißt meist strike a balance, nicht make a balance.

items.def: to arrive at an agreement that everyone accepts
items.ex: We hope to reach a consensus before the steering committee meets.
items.why: Einen Konsens „erzielen“ heißt reach a consensus, nicht make a consensus.

items.def: to satisfy a condition that has been set
items.ex: Our archive can meet a requirement like GoBD without extra tools.
items.why: Eine Anforderung „erfüllen“ heißt meet a requirement, nicht fill a requirement.

items.def: to make a danger or problem less serious
items.ex: A phased rollout helps us mitigate a risk before it becomes a problem.
items.why: Ein Risiko „abschwächen“ heißt mitigate a risk; weaken a risk klingt unnatürlich.

items.def: to think carefully about the good and bad sides of each choice
items.ex: Let us weigh the options before we commit to a vendor.
items.why: Abwägen heißt das Verb weigh, nicht das Nomen weight: weigh the options.

items.def: to create an example that others will expect to follow
items.ex: A discount this large would set a precedent for every other customer.
items.why: Einen Präzedenzfall „schaffen“ heißt set a precedent, nicht make a precedent.

items.def: to win the support of the people who must agree
items.ex: Our first goal is to secure buy-in from the finance team.
items.why: „Rückhalt sichern“ heißt secure buy-in; buy-in ist die Zustimmung, kein Kauf.

items.def: to make more people start using a product or tool
items.ex: A short training plan can drive adoption across all departments.
items.why: „Nutzung vorantreiben“ heißt drive adoption, nicht push the usage.

items.def: to make a process simpler and faster by removing unnecessary steps
items.ex: The new workflow lets us streamline a process that used to take weeks.
items.why: Streamline a process heißt „vereinfachen und beschleunigen“; das Nomen dazu ist streamlining.

items.def: to help people work together better
items.ex: Shared dashboards foster collaboration between sales and support.
items.why: Foster ist förmlicher als support oder promote und passt in Berichte und Pitches.

items.def: to keep to the schedule that was agreed
items.ex: We will stick to the timeline unless the client changes the scope.
items.why: Einen Zeitplan „einhalten“ heißt stick to oder keep to the timeline, nicht hold the timeline.

items.def: to be later than planned
items.ex: If we fall behind schedule, the launch date moves into January.
items.why: „In Verzug geraten“ heißt fall behind schedule, nicht get in delay.

items.def: to meet problems that slow you down
items.ex: We did not expect to run into obstacles this early in the project.
items.why: „Auf Hindernisse stoßen“ heißt run into obstacles, nicht bump on obstacles.

items.def: to start to succeed and attract more interest or users
items.ex: The new product line is starting to gain traction in the DACH region.
items.why: „An Fahrt gewinnen“ im Geschäft heißt gain traction (oder gain momentum), nicht win speed.

items.def: to prepare the arguments and numbers that justify an investment
items.ex: We still have to build a business case for the cloud migration.
items.why: Build a business case heißt „erarbeiten“; make the case for heißt „überzeugend vortragen“.

items.def: to give strong reasons that make others agree
items.ex: You need to make a compelling case for the extra budget.
items.why: Make a case for heißt „Argumente vortragen“; compelling heißt „zwingend überzeugend“.

items.def: to be better than people hoped
items.ex: Our goal is to exceed expectations in the first ninety days.
items.why: Erwartungen „übertreffen“ heißt exceed expectations, nicht overtake.

items.def: to accept that something is your job and make sure it gets done
items.ex: Someone has to take ownership of the data migration.
items.why: Take ownership betont die Zuständigkeit; take responsibility betont eher Pflicht oder Schuld.

items.def: to reduce a difference until it disappears
items.ex: This update will close the gap between our offer and the market.
items.why: Eine Lücke „schließen“ heißt close the gap, nicht shut.

items.def: to make sure someone always gets the latest information
items.ex: Please keep me in the loop on any changes to the contract.
items.why: „Auf dem Laufenden halten“ heißt keep sb in the loop (auch: keep sb posted), nicht hold up to date.

items.def: to do what you promised
items.ex: We always honor a commitment once it is in writing.
items.why: Eine Zusage „einhalten“ heißt honor a commitment (oder keep a promise), nicht hold a commitment.

items.def: to be a possible source of danger or loss
items.ex: An unclear data policy can pose a risk for the whole project.
items.why: Ein Risiko „darstellen“ heißt pose (oder present) a risk, nicht put a risk.

items.def: to produce a useful or positive outcome
items.ex: The pilot should yield results within six weeks.
items.why: Yield ist förmlicher als bring: yield results, yield returns.

items.def: used to add a point that limits what you just said
items.ex: The license fee is higher. That said, the total cost over three years is lower.
items.why: Mit that said schränkt man das Vorige ein; es steht am Satzanfang, danach ein Komma.

items.def: used to introduce a contrasting point
items.ex: Cloud is faster to deploy. On the other hand, some customers want full control.
items.why: On the other hand folgt fast immer auf on the one hand oder eine erste Aussage.

items.def: used to give a final overall view
items.ex: All in all, the pilot went better than we expected.
items.why: All in all fasst zusammen; es steht meist am Satzanfang, danach ein Komma.

items.def: used to add a point that is fair to the other side
items.ex: To be fair, the first version had no audit trail either.
items.why: To be fair gibt der Gegenseite recht und mildert Kritik.

items.en: as far as I can tell
items.def: used when you are fairly sure but not certain
items.ex: As far as I can tell, the contract does not cover backups.
items.why: As far as I can tell heißt „soweit ich sehen kann“ und klingt sachlicher als I think.

items.def: used to say politely what you would probably choose
items.ex: I would be inclined to wait until we see the second quarter numbers.
items.why: Would be inclined to + Verb mildert eine Empfehlung ab und klingt förmlich.

items.def: used to give your view in a careful way
items.ex: It seems to me that the real issue is the integration, not the price.
items.why: It seems to me that leitet eine vorsichtige Meinung ein; danach folgt ein ganzer Satz.

items.def: a polite way to ask permission to say something
items.ex: If I may, I would like to add one point about the timeline.
items.why: If I may ist höflich-förmlich; im Meeting oft vor einem Einwurf.

items.en: let me push back on that
items.def: a polite but clear way to disagree
items.ex: Let me push back on that a little: the data does not show a drop in usage.
items.why: Let me push back on that widerspricht höflich; deutlicher als „I am not sure“, freundlicher als „you are wrong“.

items.en: I see where you are coming from
items.def: used to show understanding before you disagree
items.ex: I see where you are coming from, but the budget is fixed for this year.
items.why: Dieser Satz zeigt Verständnis; erst danach kommt das „but“.

items.def: used to link a decision to what was just said
items.ex: With that in mind, I suggest we start with a small pilot.
items.why: With that in mind verbindet einen Vorschlag mit dem, was gerade gesagt wurde.

items.def: used to say that something does not change your point
items.ex: Be that as it may, we still need a signed order by Friday.
items.why: Be that as it may ist förmlich; nicht „as it may be“.

items.def: used to say that you consider new facts
items.ex: In light of the new regulation, we need to update the contract.
items.why: In light of + Nomen heißt „angesichts“ (ähnlich: in view of).

items.def: used to talk about what will happen from now on
items.ex: Moving forward, every project will have a named owner.
items.why: Moving forward heißt „ab jetzt, künftig“, nicht „vorwärtsbewegen“.

items.def: used for a temporary situation
items.ex: For the time being, we will keep both systems running.
items.why: For the time being heißt „vorerst“, nicht at the time being.

items.en: would it be fair to say
items.def: used to check whether you understood correctly
items.ex: Would it be fair to say that price is your main concern?
items.why: Would it be fair to say fasst vorsichtig zusammen und lädt zum Korrigieren ein.

items.en: let me take a step back
items.de: lassen Sie mich kurz einen Schritt zurücktreten
items.def: used to look at the bigger picture again
items.ex: Let me take a step back and look at the overall goal.
items.why: Take a step back ist bildlich gemeint: kurz Abstand nehmen, nicht „zurückgehen“.

items.def: used to explain the same idea in other words
items.ex: To put it differently, we cannot sign before legal has reviewed it.
items.why: To put it differently leitet eine Umformulierung ein, nicht „in other words“ ersetzen.

items.def: used to repeat what the other person seems to say
items.ex: What I am hearing is that integration matters more than price.
items.why: What I am hearing is zeigt aktives Zuhören; danach folgt die eigene Zusammenfassung.

items.def: used to return to a topic that you left earlier
items.ex: Let us circle back to pricing once we agree on the scope.
items.why: Circle back to ist US-Business-Sprache für „später wieder aufgreifen“.

items.de: sich wehren gegen, Einwände erheben gegen
items.def: to disagree with or resist something
items.ex: The customer started to push back on the price right away.
items.why: Push back on = widersprechen; formeller: object to oder challenge.

items.def: to investigate a question or problem
items.ex: We will look into the issue and get back to you by Friday.
items.why: Look into ist die Gesprächsform von investigate; in der E-Mail klingt investigate förmlicher.

items.def: to take further action after an earlier contact
items.ex: I will follow up on the open items after the call.
items.why: Follow up on heißt „zu einem Thema nachfassen“; follow up with sb heißt „bei jemandem nachhaken“.

items.def: to give official approval
items.ex: Legal still needs to sign off on the final contract.
items.why: Sign off on ist die Gesprächsform von approve.

items.def: to solve small remaining problems
items.ex: We still need to iron out a few details in the contract.
items.why: Iron out ist informeller als resolve; es passt zu kleinen Details.

items.def: to introduce something step by step
items.ex: We plan to roll out the new portal in March.
items.why: Roll out ist die Gesprächsform von launch oder implement.

items.def: to make something bigger as demand grows
items.ex: The platform can scale up quickly when the load increases.
items.why: Scale up ist das Gegenteil von scale down; formeller: expand.

items.def: to stop using something gradually
items.ex: We will phase out the old interface by the end of the year.
items.why: Phase out = schrittweise abschaffen; formeller: discontinue.

items.def: to get involved to help or to solve a problem
items.ex: If the project slips, our director will step in.
items.why: Step in heißt „einspringen“ oder „eingreifen“, ohne Ort danach.

items.def: to finish something
items.ex: Let us wrap up the meeting with a quick summary.
items.why: Wrap up ist die Gesprächsform von conclude.

items.de: sich melden bei, Kontakt aufnehmen mit
items.def: to contact someone, often to offer or ask for help
items.ex: Please reach out to our support team if you need help.
items.why: Reach out to ist freundlicher als contact; im Kundengespräch sehr üblich.

items.def: to move something to an earlier time
items.ex: Can we bring forward the demo by one week?
items.why: Bring forward = vorziehen; das Gegenteil ist push back = verschieben.

items.def: a situation where you must give up one good thing to get another
items.ex: There is always a trade-off between speed and quality.

items.def: something that limits what you can do
items.ex: Budget is our biggest constraint for this year.

items.def: to make something bad less serious
items.ex: Regular backups mitigate the risk of data loss.

items.def: to be more important or bigger than something else
items.ex: In our calculation, the long-term savings outweigh the one-time setup cost.

items.def: possible to do in practice
items.ex: A full migration in one month is not feasible.

items.def: able to work successfully, especially in business
items.ex: We need a viable plan before we ask for more budget.

items.def: to use something you have to get a better result
items.ex: We can leverage our existing partners to enter the new market.

items.def: to make a process or system simpler and more efficient
items.ex: The new tool helps us streamline our approval process.

items.def: strong and able to work well in difficult conditions
items.ex: We need a robust solution that works even during peak load.

items.def: able to grow easily when more capacity is needed
items.ex: Our cloud platform is scalable, so you only pay for what you use.

items.def: a point in a process where work slows down
items.ex: Manual approvals are the bottleneck in our invoice process.

items.def: a standard that you compare other things with
items.ex: We used the industry average as a benchmark.

items.def: the reasons that explain a decision
items.ex: Can you explain the rationale behind this price?

items.def: regular costs or extra work that do not produce direct value
items.ex: Automation reduces the administrative overhead in our finance team.

items.def: clear and real enough to be seen or measured
items.ex: The pilot gave us tangible results within a month.

items.def: the length of time that a document must be kept
items.ex: The retention period for invoices differs from country to country.

items.def: a record that shows who did what and when
items.ex: Every change leaves an audit trail that auditors can follow.

items.def: the country or region where data is physically stored
items.ex: Data residency in the EU is a must for many of our customers.

items.def: one place that holds the official version of the data
items.ex: The archive becomes the single source of truth for all contracts.

items.def: a way to give people access according to their job role
items.ex: Role-based access keeps sensitive files away from the wrong people.

items.def: a launch in several stages instead of all at once
items.ex: A phased rollout lets us fix problems before every team goes live.

items.def: an old system that is still in use
items.ex: Many customers still depend on a legacy system for their invoices.

items.def: a situation where it is very hard to switch to another supplier
items.ex: Open standards protect our customers from vendor lock-in when they switch providers.

items.def: the time during which a system is working and available
items.ex: Our contract guarantees an uptime of 99.9 percent.

items.def: a contract that defines the quality of a service, such as response times
items.ex: The service level agreement defines how fast we respond to incidents.

items.def: built so that it cannot be changed or manipulated by unauthorized people
items.ex: An audit-proof archive needs tamper-proof storage so that nobody can change old files.

items.def: the stages of a document from creation to deletion
items.ex: Good governance covers the whole document lifecycle, from scanning to deletion.

items.def: using software to run recurring steps without manual work
items.ex: Workflow automation cuts the time for invoice approval in half.

items.def: the fact of following rules and laws (verb: comply, adjective: compliant)
items.ex: Full compliance with the new rules is mandatory from 2027.

items.def: following the rules and laws (noun: compliance)
items.ex: Our archive keeps you compliant with GoBD at all times.

items.def: the quality of always behaving or looking the same way (adjective: consistent)
items.ex: Consistency across all offices makes training much easier.

items.def: always the same in quality or behavior (noun: consistency)
items.ex: We need consistent data in every system, otherwise reports contradict each other.

items.def: the quality of being dependable (adjective: reliable)
items.ex: Reliability is more important to our customers than the lowest price.

items.def: the process of starting to use something (verb: adopt)
items.ex: User adoption was higher than we had planned.

items.def: the fact that something can be used when needed (adjective: available)
items.ex: High availability is part of every enterprise contract.

items.def: working well without wasting time or money (adjective: efficient)
items.ex: The new process improves efficiency in the finance team.

items.def: to make a real difference to a result
items.ex: One more feature will not move the needle for our customers.
items.why: Move the needle = messbare Wirkung haben; oft in Verneinung: will not move the needle.

items.def: a rough number that is close enough for planning
items.ex: Can you give me a ballpark figure for the migration cost?
items.why: Ballpark figure ist eine Näherung, kein genauer Preis.

items.def: an easy opportunity that brings quick results
items.ex: Let us start with the low-hanging fruit and tackle the hard part later.
items.why: Low-hanging fruit = das Naheliegende zuerst; nicht „easy fruits“.

items.def: good for everyone who is involved
items.ex: A shared pilot would be a win-win for both companies.
items.why: A win-win ist ein Nomen oder Adjektiv: a win-win situation.

items.def: having the same understanding of a situation
items.ex: Before the call, let us make sure we are all on the same page.
items.why: On the same page = gleicher Wissensstand, nicht nur gleiche Meinung.

items.def: to offer something useful in a discussion or partnership
items.ex: Every partner should know what they bring to the table.
items.why: Bring to the table = etwas Wertvolles einbringen; nicht „bring on the table“.

items.de: zurück an den Anfang, neu planen
items.def: used when a plan failed and you must start again
items.ex: If the pilot fails, it is back to the drawing board.
items.why: Back to the drawing board = der Plan ist gescheitert; nicht zurück zum Zeichenbrett im Wortsinn.

items.def: to carry out an official check of records, systems or processes
items.ex: The external team will conduct an audit of our document retention practices in March.
items.why: Eine Prüfung „durchführen“ heißt conduct an audit, nicht make an audit.

items.def: to finish something by the agreed date
items.ex: We can only meet a deadline this tight if legal approves the contract today.
items.why: Einen Termin „einhalten“ heißt meet a deadline, nicht keep a deadline.

items.def: to fail to finish something by the agreed date
items.ex: If we miss a deadline again, the client may terminate the contract.
items.why: Einen Termin „verpassen“ heißt miss a deadline, nicht lose a deadline.

items.def: to decide something together after a discussion
items.ex: We are confident that we can reach an agreement by the end of the month.
items.why: Eine Einigung „erzielen“ heißt reach an agreement, nicht make an agreement.

items.def: to talk with a seller until you agree on a lower price
items.ex: Our procurement team managed to negotiate a discount of twelve percent for the annual license.
items.why: Einen Rabatt „aushandeln“ heißt negotiate a discount; give a discount macht der Verkäufer.

items.def: to give up something in order to reach an agreement
items.ex: Each side will have to make a concession if we want to close this quarter.
items.why: Ein Zugeständnis „machen“ heißt make a concession, nicht do a concession.

items.def: to negotiate very firmly and accept only favorable terms
items.ex: Their purchasing manager really knows how to drive a hard bargain on payment terms.
items.why: Drive a hard bargain beschreibt eine Person, die in Verhandlungen kaum nachgibt.

items.def: to complete a negotiation and agree on a sale or contract
items.ex: It took us six months to close a deal with such a large customer.
items.why: Einen Vertrag oder Verkauf „abschließen“ heißt close a deal, nicht finish a deal.

items.def: to formally send a written offer or plan for approval
items.ex: We need to submit a proposal to the city council before the end of next week.
items.why: Einreichen heißt submit. Give in bedeutet „nachgeben“ und passt hier nicht.

items.def: to prepare the written text of a legal agreement
items.ex: Our legal department will draw up a contract as soon as the terms are final.
items.why: Einen Vertrag „aufsetzen“ heißt draw up a contract, nicht build a contract.

items.def: to officially end a legal agreement before or at its end date
items.ex: Either party may terminate a contract with three months' written notice.
items.why: Einen Vertrag „kündigen“ heißt terminate a contract. Das klingt förmlicher als cancel.

items.def: to fail to do what a legal agreement requires
items.ex: Delivering late again could mean that we breach a contract signed last year.
items.why: Gegen einen Vertrag „verstoßen“ heißt breach a contract, nicht injure a contract.

items.def: to make sure that people actually follow a rule
items.ex: It is difficult to enforce a policy that nobody has ever explained properly.
items.why: Eine Richtlinie „durchsetzen“ heißt enforce a policy. Push through heißt „durchboxen“ und meint etwas anderes.

items.def: to follow the rules set by law or by an authority
items.ex: All our systems must comply with regulations on data protection in every country we serve.
items.why: Nach comply folgt with: comply with regulations, nicht comply regulations.

items.def: to make certain that rules and laws are followed
items.ex: The new workflow helps us ensure compliance without slowing down the sales team.
items.why: Die Einhaltung „sicherstellen“ heißt ensure compliance, nicht secure compliance.

items.def: to satisfy the auditors that your records and processes are correct
items.ex: We were relieved to pass an audit that had worried us for months.
items.why: Eine Prüfung „bestehen“ heißt pass an audit, das Gegenteil ist fail an audit.

items.def: to deal with a customer's report of a problem
items.ex: Our support team is trained to handle a complaint calmly and within one working day.
items.why: Eine Beschwerde „bearbeiten“ heißt handle a complaint, nicht work a complaint.

items.def: to find a solution to a disagreement between parties
items.ex: The two companies agreed to resolve a dispute over fees through mediation.
items.why: Einen Streit „beilegen“ heißt resolve a dispute, nicht solve a dispute.

items.def: to pass a problem to someone with more authority
items.ex: If the vendor does not respond today, we will have to escalate an issue this serious to management.
items.why: Im Business-Englisch heißt escalate neutral „an die nächste Ebene weitergeben“, nicht „eskalieren lassen“ im Sinne von verschärfen.

items.def: to decide how people, time or money will be divided among tasks
items.ex: We should allocate resources to the migration before we start any new project.
items.why: Allocate betont das gezielte Zuteilen. Distribute klingt eher nach gleichmäßig verteilen.

items.def: to make sure people have sensible ideas about what will happen
items.ex: It is important to manage expectations early so that nobody is surprised by the schedule.
items.why: Erwartungen „steuern“ heißt manage expectations, nicht control expectations.

items.def: to give a talk with slides to an audience
items.ex: She will deliver a presentation to the board on Thursday morning.
items.why: Give a presentation ist am häufigsten. Deliver klingt etwas förmlicher. Hold a presentation ist die typische Fehlübersetzung.

items.def: to postpone making a choice until a later time
items.ex: The committee voted to defer a decision until the cost estimates are available.
items.why: Defer ist förmlicher als postpone und passt zu Gremien: eine Entscheidung auf später verschieben.

items.def: to lead a formal meeting and keep it organized
items.ex: Maria will chair a meeting of the project board next Monday.
items.why: Eine Sitzung „leiten“ heißt chair a meeting, nicht lead a meeting im formellen Kontext.

items.def: to write down what is said and decided in a meeting
items.ex: Could you take minutes today, because I need to present the first item?
items.why: Ein Protokoll „führen“ heißt take minutes, nicht write a protocol.

items.def: to deal successfully with a reason someone gives for not agreeing
items.ex: To overcome an objection about price, we showed the total savings over five years.
items.why: Einen Einwand „entkräften“ heißt overcome an objection, nicht defeat an objection.

items.def: to deliver the goods or services that a customer has ordered
items.ex: We are unable to fulfill an order of this size before the end of May.
items.why: Eine Bestellung „ausführen“ heißt fulfill an order, nicht execute an order im Alltag.

items.def: to officially force a limit on what people may do
items.ex: The regulator decided to impose a restriction on how long personal data may be stored.
items.why: Eine Einschränkung „auferlegen“ heißt impose a restriction, nicht put on a restriction.

items.def: to give someone permission to enter or use a system or file
items.ex: Only an administrator can grant access to the archive of signed contracts.
items.why: Zugriff „gewähren“ heißt grant access, nicht give an access.

items.def: to take away someone's permission to use a system
items.ex: When an employee leaves, IT must revoke access to all company systems immediately.
items.why: Zugriff „entziehen“ heißt revoke access, nicht withdraw access.

items.def: to put a chosen plan or product into practice
items.ex: It will take at least a quarter to implement a solution of this complexity.
items.why: Eine Lösung „umsetzen“ heißt implement a solution, nicht realize a solution.

items.def: to test a new idea or system on a small scale first
items.ex: Before the full rollout, we will run a pilot in the Munich office.
items.why: Einen Pilotversuch „durchführen“ heißt run a pilot, nicht make a pilot.

items.def: to collect opinions and reactions from users or customers
items.ex: We plan to gather feedback from the first ten customers before changing the design.
items.why: Rückmeldungen „einholen“ heißt gather feedback; feedback ist unzählbar, also kein feedbacks.

items.def: to include other people's comments in an improved version
items.ex: Thank you for your comments. We will incorporate feedback from all teams in the next draft.
items.why: Rückmeldungen „einarbeiten“ heißt incorporate feedback, nicht work in feedback.

items.def: to follow and record how far something has developed
items.ex: The dashboard allows managers to track progress across all migration projects in real time.
items.why: Den Fortschritt „verfolgen“ heißt track progress, nicht follow progress.

items.def: to judge what effect a change will have
items.ex: We need to assess the impact on existing customers before we change the pricing.
items.why: Die Auswirkungen „bewerten“ heißt assess the impact; impact ist hier ein Substantiv.

items.def: to be the one who pays for something
items.ex: The supplier agreed to bear the cost of any repairs during the first year.
items.why: Die Kosten „tragen“ heißt bear the cost, nicht carry the cost.

items.def: to reduce the amount of money spent
items.ex: Management has asked every department to cut costs by five percent this year.
items.why: Kosten „senken“ heißt cut costs oder reduce costs, nicht lower down costs.

items.def: to spend more money than was planned
items.ex: Any decision that would exceed the budget must be approved by the finance director.
items.why: Das Budget „überschreiten“ heißt exceed the budget, nicht overstep the budget.

items.def: to spend no more money than was planned
items.ex: The project was delivered on time and managed to stay within budget.
items.why: Im Budget „bleiben“ heißt stay within budget, nicht stay in the budget.

items.def: to achieve a planned number or result
items.ex: The sales team is on track to hit a target that looked impossible in January.
items.why: Hit oder meet a target sind die üblichen Verben für Zahlenziele. Reach geht auch, klingt aber weniger geschäftlich.

items.def: to arrive at an important point in a project
items.ex: We will celebrate when we reach a milestone like the first successful go-live.
items.why: Reach a milestone ist die Standardform. Achieve a milestone geht auch, klingt aber nach Erfolg.

items.def: to prepare the basic conditions for something later
items.ex: This workshop will lay the groundwork for the migration that starts in the autumn.
items.why: Die Grundlage „schaffen“ heißt lay the groundwork, nicht create the ground.

items.def: to create energy and progress that keeps growing
items.ex: A few early successes will help us build momentum across the whole organization.
items.why: Schwung „aufbauen“ heißt build momentum; momentum ist unzählbar.

items.def: to slow down after a period of good progress
items.ex: The project began to lose momentum once the key sponsor left the company.
items.why: An Schwung „verlieren“ heißt lose momentum, nicht lose the swing.

items.def: to decide what something means after looking at the facts
items.ex: It is too early to draw a conclusion from just two weeks of data.
items.why: Einen Schluss „ziehen“ heißt draw a conclusion, nicht pull a conclusion.

items.def: to adopt a clear position on an issue
items.ex: The company decided to take a stance against unclear data practices.
items.why: Eine Haltung „einnehmen“ heißt take a stance; take a position ist ähnlich.

items.def: to formally suggest what should be done
items.ex: Based on the analysis, I would like to make a recommendation on the vendor.
items.why: Eine Empfehlung „aussprechen“ heißt make a recommendation; wörtlich say oder pronounce a recommendation passt nicht.

items.def: to start concentrating on something different
items.ex: Let us shift the focus from features to the actual needs of our users.
items.why: Den Schwerpunkt „verlagern“ heißt shift the focus, nicht move the focus point.

items.def: to decide which topics will be discussed
items.ex: The chairperson will set the agenda and send it out two days in advance.
items.why: Die Tagesordnung „festlegen“ heißt set the agenda; agenda ist im Englischen die Themenliste.

items.def: used to add a point that follows from the same logic
items.ex: Customers expect fast answers; by the same token, they expect those answers to be correct.
items.why: By the same token knüpft logisch an die vorige Aussage an; es ist formeller als also.

items.def: used to say that something is partly true
items.ex: To some extent, the delay was caused by changes we requested ourselves.
items.why: To some extent heißt „teilweise“ und schwächt eine Aussage ab. Ohne diese Wendung klingt sie zu absolut.

items.def: used to talk about what will happen over a long period of time, not just now
items.ex: In the long run, automating this process will save us considerable time and money.
items.why: In the long run heißt auf lange Sicht, nicht in the long term run.

items.def: used to give a more exact version of what you just said
items.ex: We lost several customers last year, or to be more precise, four of our ten largest.
items.why: Mit to be more precise korrigiert oder präzisiert man sich selbst, ohne unhöflich zu sein.

items.def: used to describe the situation as it is now, without changes
items.ex: As it stands, the proposal does not meet our security requirements.
items.why: As it stands bezieht sich auf den aktuellen Zustand, nicht auf eine Meinung.

items.def: used after weighing different points to give your overall view
items.ex: On balance, I think the second option is the safer choice for us.
items.why: On balance = nach Abwägen aller Punkte, nicht „in balance“ (im Gleichgewicht).

items.def: used to talk about the past with what you know now
items.ex: In hindsight, we should have tested the migration with a smaller group.
items.why: In hindsight steht ohne the und heißt „im Rückblick, mit dem Wissen von heute“. Afterwards heißt nur „danach“.

items.def: used to introduce a short summary of what was said
items.ex: To sum up, we need more time, a larger budget and a clear owner.
items.why: To sum up beendet einen Beitrag; in schriftlichen Texten auch in summary.

items.def: used to explain something more clearly to avoid confusion
items.ex: Let me clarify what I meant, because my last email was not precise.
items.why: Let me clarify ist höflicher als you misunderstood me.

items.def: used to draw attention to an important or interesting fact
items.ex: It is worth noting that the cheapest option also has the longest delivery time.
items.why: Nach it is worth noting that folgt ein vollständiger Satz mit Subjekt und Verb.

items.def: used to introduce the subject you are about to talk about
items.ex: With regard to your question about pricing, I will send details tomorrow.
items.why: With regard to ist formell und steht im Singular: regard, nicht regards.

items.def: used to say what usually happens
items.ex: As a rule, we answer all support requests within four working hours.
items.why: As a rule heißt in der Regel, nicht by rule.

items.def: used to say that something will only happen if a condition is met
items.ex: We can deliver on Friday, provided that the specifications are final today.
items.why: Provided that leitet eine Bedingung ein, ähnlich wie if, aber strenger.

items.def: used politely when you think you know something but are not completely sure
items.ex: Unless I am mistaken, the contract expires at the end of June.
items.why: Unless I am mistaken sichert die eigene Aussage höflich ab (Hedging). Es korrigiert nicht den anderen.

items.def: used to say that something does not depend on something else
items.ex: Regardless of the outcome, we will keep working with this supplier.
items.why: Regardless of ist richtig; irregardless gilt als falsch.

items.def: used to talk about what will happen if something occurs
items.ex: In the event of a system failure, the backup site takes over automatically.
items.why: In the event of steht vor einem Substantiv, nicht vor einem Satz.

items.def: used to say that something is mostly true
items.ex: By and large, the feedback from our customers has been very positive.
items.why: By and large ist eine feste Wendung; man ändert kein Wort daran.

items.def: used to talk about the present point in a process
items.ex: At this stage, it would be premature to commit to a final date.
items.why: At this stage klingt professioneller als at the moment, wenn es um Prozesse geht.

items.def: used to say that one thing is not included
items.ex: With the exception of two small items, all requirements have been fulfilled.
items.why: With the exception of steht vor dem Ausgenommenen; exception ist ein Substantiv.

items.def: used to introduce your personal view of a situation
items.ex: From my perspective, the biggest risk is the lack of a clear owner.
items.why: From my perspective ist weicher als I think und passt gut in Meetings.

items.en: I would like to point out
items.def: used to politely draw attention to a fact
items.ex: I would like to point out that the deadline in the contract is binding.
items.why: I would like to point out leitet höflich eine wichtige Information ein, die der andere übersehen könnte.

items.def: used to add a surprising or correcting detail
items.ex: As a matter of fact, we already ran a similar pilot two years ago.
items.why: As a matter of fact ist feststehend. Es ergänzt eine überraschende oder berichtigende Tatsache. Für ein einfaches „tatsächlich“ genügt in fact.

items.def: to do and complete a planned piece of work
items.ex: We will carry out a full security test before the system goes live.
items.why: Carry out ist ein trennbares Verb; mit Objekt: carry out a test, carry it out.

items.def: to tell someone something they may not have noticed
items.ex: Thank you for taking the time to point out the error in the invoice.
items.why: Point out kann man trennen: point the problem out; Pronomen gehören dazwischen.

items.def: to mention a topic for discussion
items.ex: She decided to bring up the budget problem at the end of the meeting.
items.why: Bring up heißt ein Thema zur Sprache bringen und ist trennbar: bring it up. Bring up a child heißt „aufziehen“.

items.def: to decide that something is not possible or not suitable
items.ex: We cannot rule out a delay if the supplier does not confirm the date.
items.why: Rule out ist trennbar: rule the option out, rule it out.

items.def: to support a statement with evidence
items.ex: Can you back up your estimate with figures from previous projects?
items.why: Back up bedeutet hier belegen; das Substantiv backup (eine Sicherung) schreibt man zusammen.

items.def: to give responsibility or control to someone else
items.ex: Before she goes on leave, she will hand over all her projects to Tom.
items.why: Hand over ist trennbar: hand the project over; das Substantiv ist handover.

items.def: to do what you said you would do
items.ex: It is easy to make promises, but harder to follow through on them.
items.why: Follow through on braucht on: follow through on a promise, nicht follow through a promise.

items.def: to solve a problem or organize a confusing situation
items.ex: We need to sort out the licensing question before the audit starts.
items.why: Sort out ist umgangssprachlicher als resolve und sehr gebräuchlich.

items.def: to include something when you calculate or plan
items.ex: Please factor in two weeks for testing when you plan the schedule.
items.why: Factor in ist trennbar: factor the costs in; es heißt einkalkulieren.

items.def: to choose one option from several
items.ex: Most customers opt for the annual plan because it is cheaper.
items.why: Opt for braucht for; opt to ist mit einem Verb möglich: opt to wait.

items.def: to accept and support an idea or plan
items.ex: The project will only succeed if the whole team can buy into the new process.
items.why: Buy into hat hier nichts mit Kaufen zu tun, sondern mit Überzeugtsein.

items.def: to reduce the amount of something you use or spend
items.ex: We will have to cut back on travel until the end of the year.
items.why: Cut back on braucht on vor dem Objekt: cut back on costs.

items.def: to fail to happen, usually because of a problem
items.ex: We must act now, or the whole plan could fall through at the last minute.
items.why: Fall through beschreibt Pläne, die nicht zustande kommen; es hat kein Objekt.

items.def: to think of an idea or a solution
items.ex: The team needs to come up with a solution before the customer calls tomorrow.
items.why: Come up with braucht with: come up with an idea, nicht come up an idea.

items.def: to delay doing something until later
items.ex: Let us hold off on the announcement until the contract is signed.
items.why: Hold off on braucht on vor dem Objekt; hold off allein heißt warten.

items.def: to make something seem less important than it is
items.ex: He tried to play down the risks, but the auditors saw the problems.
items.why: Play down ist trennbar: play the risks down; es ist das Gegenteil von play up.

items.def: to reduce the number of possibilities
items.ex: We managed to narrow down the list of vendors to three companies.
items.why: Narrow down heißt eingrenzen, nicht make narrow.

items.def: to notice something that is not obvious and understand its meaning
items.ex: Good salespeople pick up on small signals from the customer during a call.
items.why: Pick up on heißt etwas bemerken oder aufgreifen; es hat hier nichts mit Abholen zu tun.

items.def: the quality of having more than one possible meaning
items.ex: The ambiguity in the contract wording led to a long argument about the delivery date.

items.def: a plan or amount of money for something unexpected
items.ex: We should include a contingency of ten percent in the project budget.

items.def: a difference between two things that should be the same
items.ex: There is a discrepancy between the invoice and the original purchase order.

items.def: legal responsibility for damage or debt
items.ex: The contract limits the supplier's liability to the value of the order.

items.def: the fact of being responsible for your decisions and actions
items.ex: Clear accountability for each task prevents delays and endless discussions.

items.def: a product or document that must be provided at the end of a task
items.ex: The first deliverable is a detailed project plan due on Monday.

items.def: something that must exist or happen before something else can
items.ex: A completed security review is a prerequisite for the final approval.

items.def: a rule or measure that protects against harm or loss
items.ex: The system includes a safeguard against accidental deletion of contracts.

items.def: the act of supervising something, or a mistake caused by not noticing
items.ex: The board is responsible for oversight of all major financial decisions.

items.def: done completely and with great attention to detail
items.ex: We carried out a thorough review of every contract in the archive.

items.def: giving all the necessary information in few words
items.ex: Please keep your summary concise, because the committee has very little time.

items.def: dealing with problems in a practical and sensible way
items.ex: We chose a pragmatic approach and started with the most urgent processes.

items.def: not final or certain, and open to change
items.ex: We have a tentative agreement, but the legal team still needs to review it.

items.def: large in amount, importance or value
items.ex: The new system will bring substantial savings in storage and handling costs.

items.def: so small that it is not worth considering
items.ex: The extra cost for the upgrade is negligible compared to the potential savings.

items.def: about to happen very soon
items.ex: A decision on the tender is imminent, so please keep your phones on.

items.def: paying extreme attention to small details
items.ex: Her meticulous documentation made the audit much easier for everyone.

items.def: not willing to do something and slow to agree to it
items.ex: The client was reluctant to share the data without a signed confidentiality agreement.

items.def: including all or nearly all the elements of something
items.ex: We offer a comprehensive solution that covers scanning, storage and long-term archiving.

items.def: used when you believe something can be supported with good reasons
items.ex: This is arguably the most important decision we will make this year.

items.def: mainly or mostly
items.ex: Our customers are predominantly mid-sized companies in the manufacturing sector.

items.def: used to point out an important example
items.ex: Several departments, notably finance and legal, have asked for earlier access.

items.def: to publicly say that you support something
items.ex: The steering committee decided to endorse the proposal for the new archive.

items.def: to weaken something gradually
items.ex: Constant changes to the scope will undermine the trust of the project team.

items.def: to put something at risk of being harmed or lost
items.ex: A single security incident could jeopardize our relationship with this customer.

items.def: to make two different things fit together or agree
items.ex: It is hard to reconcile the two sets of figures in these reports.

items.def: to make room for or adapt to someone's needs
items.ex: The new platform can accommodate up to ten thousand users at the same time.

items.def: to make a process happen faster
items.ex: We can expedite the delivery if you confirm the order before noon.

items.def: data that describes other data, such as author, date or type
items.ex: Good metadata makes it possible to find any document within a few seconds.

items.def: a system that records changes to a document or file over time
items.ex: Version control ensures that nobody accidentally works on an outdated draft.

items.def: the process of moving data from one system to another
items.ex: The data migration will take place over a weekend to avoid any downtime.

items.def: electronic data attached to a document that shows who signed it
items.ex: In the EU, an electronic signature is valid for many contracts, and a qualified one equals a handwritten signature.

items.def: the rules that decide who may see or use certain information
items.ex: Strict access control protects confidential documents from unauthorized users.

items.def: the process of turning data into a code to keep it private
items.ex: All documents are protected by encryption, both in storage and during transfer.

items.def: the plan and process for restoring systems after a serious failure
items.ex: Our disaster recovery plan guarantees that we can restore all data within four hours.

items.def: extra copies or components that take over if one fails
items.ex: The system has built-in redundancy, so a single server failure causes no data loss.

items.def: the ability of different systems to work together
items.ex: Interoperability with our existing ERP system was a key requirement in the tender.

items.de: Data Governance (Regeln und Zuständigkeiten für Daten)
items.def: the rules and responsibilities for managing data in an organization
items.ex: Without clear data governance, every department keeps its own version of the truth.

items.def: the control of documents from creation to final disposal
items.ex: Good records management reduces legal risk and makes audits much less stressful.

items.def: software that converts scanned images of text into searchable text
items.ex: Optical character recognition turns paper invoices into searchable data automatically.

items.def: the process of organizing data so it can be found quickly
items.ex: Automatic indexing saves the archive team several hours of manual work every week.

items.def: a search that looks through the entire content of documents
items.ex: With full-text search, users can find a clause in thousands of contracts instantly.

items.def: the structured approach to helping people adopt a new way of working
items.ex: Poor change management is a common reason why new systems are rejected.

items.def: a small test that shows an idea can work in practice
items.ex: We built a proof of concept in two weeks to convince management.

items.def: a period during which a system is not available
items.ex: Planned downtime will be announced at least a week in advance.

items.def: a copy of data kept in case the original is lost
items.ex: Please make sure that a backup is created before we install the update.

items.def: to set a higher standard for quality or performance
items.ex: The new competitor wants to raise the bar for customer service in our industry.
items.why: Raise the bar heißt, den Maßstab anzuheben: raise the bar for sb/sth.

items.def: to start a process or activity
items.ex: Let us get the ball rolling with a short kickoff call on Monday.
items.why: Get the ball rolling meint den Anfang; es passt gut in Meetings, ist aber locker.

items.def: to make brief contact to exchange news or check the status
items.ex: I would like to touch base with you next week about the contract.
items.why: Touch base ist ein amerikanischer Ausdruck für ein kurzes Gespräch, nicht für ein langes Treffen.

items.def: to do something in a cheaper or faster way and lose quality
items.ex: We refuse to cut corners when it comes to the security of customer data.
items.why: Cut corners ist meist negativ und beschreibt mangelnde Sorgfalt.

items.def: not currently a priority, but not forgotten
items.ex: The new feature is on the back burner until the migration is complete.
items.why: On the back burner sagt, dass etwas später bearbeitet wird, nicht dass es gestrichen ist.

items.def: to start something and work effectively from the first moment
items.ex: With strong onboarding, new colleagues can hit the ground running in their first week.
items.why: Hit the ground running beschreibt einen Start ohne Anlaufzeit.

items.def: to fail to do something that you were responsible for
items.ex: Please do not drop the ball on this quote, because it has to go out this week.
items.why: Drop the ball = eine Aufgabe versäumen, für die man zuständig war. Das klingt locker und wirkt gegenüber Kunden schnell zu salopp.

items.def: the most important fact or final result of a discussion
items.ex: The bottom line is that this solution costs less and works better.
items.why: The bottom line kommt oft am Ende und hat mit der Gewinnzeile zu tun.

items.de: viel Einarbeitung nötig, am Anfang schwer zu lernen
items.def: a situation in which something is difficult to learn at first and takes a lot of effort
items.ex: The new system has a steep learning curve, so we are planning extra training.
items.why: Achtung: Im Deutschen heißt „steile Lernkurve“ schnelles Lernen. Im Business-Englisch meint a steep learning curve meist: am Anfang viel Mühe.

items.def: openness and clarity about how decisions are made (adjective: transparent)
items.ex: Transparency about pricing builds trust with customers from the very first meeting.

items.def: a formal discussion to reach an agreement (verb: negotiate, adjective: negotiable)
items.ex: The negotiation lasted three days, but both sides left satisfied with the result.

items.def: the process of putting a plan into action (verb: implement)
items.ex: The implementation of the new archive is scheduled to start in January.

items.def: official permission to do something (verb: authorize, adjective: authorized)
items.ex: You need written authorization from your manager to access these files.

items.def: the ability to continue without harming resources (adjective: sustainable)
items.ex: Sustainability is now a key criterion in every tender we respond to.

items.def: to make people notice something
items.ex: I would like to draw attention to the revised deadline in the second row.
items.why: Aufmerksam machen „auf“ heißt draw attention to, nicht draw attention on.

items.def: to mention a subject so that others can discuss it
items.ex: Sorry to interrupt, but may I raise a point about the budget?
items.why: Raise = ansprechen; rise (steigen) hat kein Objekt und passt hier nicht.

items.def: to decide something after thinking about it
items.ex: The board will make a decision on the merger next week.
items.why: Im amerikanischen Englisch trifft man eine Entscheidung mit make, nicht mit take.

items.def: to consider something when making a decision
items.ex: Please take into account the extra shipping costs in your estimate.
items.why: Berücksichtigen heißt take into account, nicht consider in account.

items.def: to decide the last date by which something must be done
items.ex: The client set a deadline of Friday for the final draft.
items.why: Eine Frist „setzen“ heißt set a deadline, nicht put a deadline.

items.def: to organize and run a meeting
items.ex: We will hold a meeting with all department heads on Monday.
items.why: Ein Meeting „abhalten“ heißt hold a meeting, nicht make a meeting.

items.def: to earn enough money to pay for something
items.ex: The subscription fees barely cover the costs of the platform.
items.why: Kosten „decken“ heißt cover the costs, nicht cover up the costs.

items.def: to officially submit a written account of something
items.ex: Each manager must file a report by the end of the month.
items.why: File = einreichen; dieselbe Vokabel heißt auch „abheften“.

items.def: to make a confusing subject easier to understand
items.ex: The audit shed light on several hidden costs.
items.why: Shed light on = aufklären; bring light into the darkness wäre wörtlich übersetzt und klingt falsch.

items.def: to remember a fact when making a decision
items.ex: Bear in mind that the office is closed during the holidays.
items.why: Bear in mind = im Hinterkopf behalten; „Bedenken“ im Sinn von Zweifel wären concerns.

items.def: to get into a better position than others
items.ex: Early adoption helped us gain an advantage over our competitors.
items.why: Einen Vorteil „erlangen“ heißt gain an advantage, nicht win an advantage.

items.def: to stay effective even when conditions are difficult
items.ex: A good manager can withstand pressure without losing focus.
items.why: Withstand ist unregelmäßig: withstood, nicht withstanded.

items.def: to be especially careful
items.ex: Please exercise caution when sharing confidential files by email.
items.why: Exercise heißt hier „ausüben“, nicht „Übung“: exercise caution.

items.def: to make people less sure that something is true
items.ex: The new figures cast doubt on the original forecast.
items.why: Cast ist unregelmäßig (cast, cast, cast); cast doubt on = Zweifel an etwas wecken.

items.def: to stay at the same level as something that is changing
items.ex: Our systems cannot keep pace with the growing number of orders.
items.why: Schritt halten heißt keep pace with; nach with folgt die Sache, mit der man mithält.

items.def: to reduce the difference between two things
items.ex: The workshop helped bridge the gap between sales and engineering.
items.why: Bridge ist hier ein Verb: bridge the gap, nicht build a bridge over the gap.

items.def: to start guiding others in an activity
items.ex: Maria volunteered to take the lead on the migration project.
items.why: Take the lead = die Initiative ergreifen; mit on nennt man das Projekt.

items.def: to show how two things are different
items.ex: It is important to draw a distinction between cost and price.
items.why: Einen Unterschied „machen“ heißt draw a distinction, nicht make a difference (das heißt „etwas bewirken“).

items.def: to become completely full or fully used
items.ex: The server will reach capacity if traffic keeps growing.
items.why: Die Kapazitätsgrenze erreichen heißt reach capacity, ohne Artikel.

items.def: to say what you think openly
items.ex: Everyone should feel free to voice an opinion in this meeting.
items.why: Eine Meinung „äußert“ man mit voice oder express an opinion, nicht mit say an opinion.

items.def: to allow something that is normally against the rules
items.ex: We can make an exception this time, but not again.
items.why: Eine Ausnahme „machen“ heißt make an exception, nicht do an exception.

items.def: to get permission or the ability to enter or use something
items.ex: Only authorized staff can gain access to the archive.
items.why: Nach access folgt to, nicht on.

items.def: to begin an organized series of activities
items.ex: We will launch a campaign for the new product in March.
items.why: Man sagt launch a campaign oder run a campaign; start a campaign klingt im formellen Text schwächer.

items.def: to write down information so it is available later
items.ex: Please keep a record of all changes made to the contract.
items.why: Ein Protokoll oder Aufzeichnungen „führt“ man mit keep, nicht mit lead.

items.def: to make a difficult situation calmer
items.ex: A short break helped ease tensions during the negotiation.
items.why: ease tensions bedeutet abbauen; defuse tensions ist die schärfere Variante im Sinn von entschärfen.

items.def: to publicly state your position on an issue
items.ex: The union refused to take a stand on the proposed merger.
items.why: Stellung beziehen heißt take a stand on; danach folgt mit on das Thema.

items.def: used before saying something in a very direct way
items.ex: To put it bluntly, we cannot afford another delay.
items.why: Vorwarnung vor einer harten Aussage; bluntly (unverblümt) nicht mit blindly verwechseln.

items.def: used to introduce something that everyone already knows
items.ex: Needless to say, all customer data will be treated confidentially.
items.why: Needless to say heißt „selbstverständlich“ und steht meist am Satzanfang.

items.def: used to introduce your personal opinion
items.ex: To my mind, the second option carries fewer risks.
items.why: Statt „after my mind“ heißt es to my mind oder in my view.

items.en: as far as I am concerned
items.def: used to give your own view on a matter
items.ex: As far as I am concerned, the proposal is ready to be signed.
items.why: Nach as far as folgt I am concerned; as far as I know ist eine andere Wendung.

items.def: used to add a contrasting point after a statement
items.ex: Having said that, we should still check the numbers once more.
items.why: Having said that = trotzdem; Bedeutung wie that said, nur etwas gesprochener.

items.def: used to say that something is generally true
items.ex: On the whole, the pilot went better than expected.
items.why: On the whole ist feststehend; nicht in the whole.

items.de: für das, was es wert ist
items.def: used to offer an opinion modestly
items.ex: For what it is worth, I think the earlier version was clearer.
items.why: Bescheidener Einschub vor einer eigenen Meinung; nicht wörtlich übersetzen.

items.en: to make a long story short
items.def: used to skip details and give the main result
items.ex: To make a long story short, we lost the contract.
items.why: US-Form ist to make a long story short; to cut a long story short ist britisch.

items.def: used to refer to something said earlier
items.ex: As previously mentioned, the invoice must be paid within 30 days.
items.why: Previously klingt formeller als before; im Fließtext geht auch as I said.

items.def: used to show that you accept someone's argument
items.ex: I take your point, but the budget is fixed.
items.why: I take your point = ich gebe zu, dass Sie recht haben; kein „Wegnehmen“.

items.def: used to draw a conclusion from what was just said
items.ex: That being the case, we should postpone the launch.
items.why: Feste Verbindung mit being; nicht „that is the case“ am Satzanfang.

items.def: used to say that you are considering a fact
items.ex: In view of the recent delays, we have changed the schedule.
items.why: Angesichts heißt in view of; in front of meint räumlich „vor“.

items.def: used to specify the area you are talking about
items.ex: In terms of cost, the second supplier is clearly better.
items.why: In terms of braucht ein Nomen danach, nicht einen Nebensatz.

items.def: because of
items.ex: Owing to staff shortages, the office will close early on Friday.
items.why: Owing to = wegen; nicht mit own (besitzen) verwechseln.

items.def: used to ask how far something is true
items.ex: To what extent do these changes affect our delivery dates?
items.why: Inwieweit heißt to what extent, nicht „in how far“.

items.def: used to say that something is not available
items.ex: In the absence of clear data, we cannot decide.
items.why: In Ermangelung heißt in the absence of, nicht „in lack of“.

items.def: used to give the reason for an action
items.ex: The request was rejected on the grounds that it was incomplete.
items.why: Nach on the grounds that steht ein vollständiger Satz.

items.def: used to say that something is done to help or protect something
items.ex: In the interest of transparency, we will publish all figures.
items.why: Im Interesse von heißt in the interest of, im Singular.

items.de: rein theoretisch angenommen, nur um der Diskussion willen
items.def: used to accept an idea temporarily in a discussion
items.ex: For the sake of argument, let us assume the costs double.
items.why: sake bedeutet hier „um … willen“, nicht „Sache“.

items.en: if it is all right with you
items.def: used to politely check that someone agrees
items.ex: If it is all right with you, I will send the draft tomorrow.
items.why: Höfliche Rückfrage; nicht „if it is right to you“.

items.de: würde es Ihnen etwas ausmachen, wenn ich
items.def: used to ask politely for permission
items.ex: Would you mind if I opened the window for a moment?
items.why: Nach would you mind steht -ing oder if I plus Vergangenheit, nicht „if I will“.

items.def: used to make a request or question more polite
items.ex: I was wondering whether we could move the call to Thursday.
items.why: Höfliche Frage mit Vergangenheit; „I wonder“ klingt direkter.

items.def: used to politely introduce bad news
items.ex: I regret to inform you that your application was unsuccessful.
items.why: Regret to inform you = leider muss ich mitteilen; regret ist hier „bedauern“.

items.def: used to introduce official information
items.ex: Please be advised that the building will be closed on Monday.
items.why: Please be advised that ist förmlich; be advised hat nichts mit „beraten“ zu tun.

items.def: used in emails to refer to an earlier conversation
items.ex: Further to our call, I have attached the revised offer.
items.why: Formell und eher britisch; im US-Business üblicher: following up on our call oder as discussed on our call.

items.de: ich schreibe, um mich zu erkundigen
items.def: used at the start of a formal email to ask for information
items.ex: I am writing to inquire about the status of my order.
items.why: In den USA ist inquire üblicher als enquire.

items.en: I would appreciate it if you could
items.de: ich wäre dankbar, wenn Sie könnten
items.def: used to make a polite formal request
items.ex: I would appreciate it if you could confirm the date by Friday.
items.why: Hier fehlt oft it: appreciate it if, nicht appreciate if.

items.def: used to ask someone to do something soon without pressure
items.ex: Please call me back at your earliest convenience.
items.why: Wirkt höflicher als as soon as possible, aber fest an formelle Texte gebunden.

items.def: used when giving someone information to keep
items.ex: For your reference, I have attached last year's report.
items.why: For your reference heißt „zum Nachschlagen“, nicht „für Ihre Referenz“.

items.def: used to say that something follows what was agreed
items.ex: As per our agreement, the first payment is due on May 1.
items.why: As per ist Büro-Englisch; in Fließtexten eher according to.

items.def: used to say that something follows a rule
items.ex: All files are stored in accordance with company policy.
items.why: In accordance with heißt „gemäß“, nicht „in agreement to“.

items.def: used to say what must be done to reach a goal
items.ex: To this end, we have hired two additional analysts.
items.why: To this end steht am Satzanfang; nicht „for this end“.

items.def: used to introduce a difference
items.ex: By contrast, our competitor has cut its prices twice.
items.why: By contrast steht allein; in contrast to braucht ein Objekt.

items.def: used to introduce a topic that is connected
items.ex: On a related note, we need to update the access rules.
items.why: On a related note ist ein lockerer Übergang zu einem verwandten Thema.

items.def: used to say that you will give more detail
items.ex: Let me elaborate on why the timeline is so tight.
items.why: Elaborate on = näher ausführen; elaborate ist hier ein Verb, kein Adjektiv.

items.def: used to focus on one example
items.ex: The new tool helps, in particular, with reporting.
items.why: In particular steht oft nach einer allgemeinen Aussage; nicht „in special“.

items.def: used to emphasize that something is not true
items.ex: The project is by no means finished, so please do not announce it yet.
items.why: By no means ist bereits verneint; kein zusätzliches not.

items.def: used to add another point that strengthens the argument
items.ex: The plan is expensive, not to mention risky.
items.why: Not to mention verstärkt; nicht „not mention to“.

items.def: used to introduce a result
items.ex: As a consequence, several customers have switched providers.
items.why: As a consequence ist formeller als so.

items.def: used to add a stronger point
items.ex: What is more, the software is cheaper than the old system.
items.why: What is more ist feststehend; nicht „what more is“.

items.def: used to give the first of several reasons
items.ex: For one thing, we lack the staff to do it.
items.why: For one thing nennt einen Grund unter mehreren, nicht einen einzigen.

items.def: used to say that something is mostly true
items.ex: The delay was, to a large extent, caused by the supplier.
items.why: To a large extent ist feststehend, nicht in a large extent.

items.de: wenn ich es mir recht überlege
items.def: used when you suddenly remember or realize something
items.ex: Come to think of it, we have not heard from the client yet.
items.why: Come to think of it ist umgangssprachlich; nicht „coming to think“.

items.def: used to introduce a related topic
items.ex: Speaking of which, have you seen the new schedule?
items.why: Speaking of which greift ein gerade genanntes Thema auf.

items.de: nur damit wir uns richtig verstehen
items.def: used to check or stress a point
items.ex: Just to be clear, the offer is valid until Friday.
items.why: Just to be clear = zur Klärung, kein Vorwurf; im Deutschen entspricht es „nur damit wir uns richtig verstehen“.

items.de: lassen Sie mich das anders formulieren
items.def: used to say the same thing in a different way
items.ex: Let me rephrase that, because my first point was confusing.
items.why: Rephrase = anders formulieren; passt, wenn man sich selbst korrigiert.

items.def: used to add a side remark
items.ex: By the way, the printer on the second floor is fixed.
items.why: Für Randbemerkungen, nicht für Wichtiges; dafür besser on a related note oder one more thing.

items.def: used to show that a word is used loosely
items.ex: We are, as it were, starting from scratch.
items.why: As it were = sozusagen, förmlich; nicht mit as it was (wie es war) verwechseln.

items.def: to accept a task or responsibility
items.ex: She agreed to take on the new client without extra support.
items.why: Take on = übernehmen; take over bedeutet die Leitung ganz übernehmen.

items.def: to divide something into smaller parts
items.ex: Can you break down the costs by department?
items.why: Break down kann auch „kaputtgehen“ heißen; mit Objekt heißt es aufschlüsseln.

items.def: to leave an important position
items.ex: The chairman will step down at the end of the year.
items.why: Step down heißt von einem Amt zurücktreten; „abtreten“ oder „absteigen“ passt hier nicht.

items.def: to gain control of something
items.ex: A larger competitor wants to take over our company.
items.why: Take over = übernehmen mit Kontrolle; nicht overtake (überholen).

items.def: to arrange or establish something
items.ex: We set up a working group to review the process.
items.why: Set up = einrichten; das Nomen setup schreibt man zusammen.

items.def: to delay something until later
items.ex: We had to put off the launch by two weeks.
items.why: Put off = verschieben; kann auch „abschrecken“ heißen.

items.def: to prepare something by collecting information
items.ex: Could you pull together a short summary before noon?
items.why: Pull together heißt zügig zusammenstellen (oder an einem Strang ziehen); nicht mit „zusammenziehen“ übersetzen.

items.def: to give something to another person
items.ex: I will pass on your feedback to the product team.
items.why: Pass on = weitergeben; nicht give on.

items.def: to be as good as expected
items.ex: The new system did not live up to our expectations.
items.why: Live up to = erfüllen; nicht live to.

items.def: to contact someone to see how things are going
items.ex: I will check in with the supplier tomorrow.
items.why: Check in with = kurz nachfragen; nicht check with in.

items.def: to use something as a base for further progress
items.ex: We can build on last year's success if we keep the team together.
items.why: Build on = aufbauen auf; nicht build up on.

items.def: to improve skills you have not used for a while
items.ex: I need to brush up on my negotiation skills.
items.why: Brush up on = auffrischen; nicht brush up at.

items.def: to accept something less good than you wanted
items.ex: We had to settle for a smaller office.
items.why: Settle for = sich begnügen mit; nicht settle on (das heißt „sich entscheiden für“).

items.def: to form a part of a total, or to explain
items.ex: Exports account for sixty percent of our revenue.
items.why: Account for steht für „ausmachen“ (Anteil) und „erklären“; „account of“ oder „account about“ ist falsch.

items.def: to increase something quickly
items.ex: We plan to ramp up production in the spring.
items.why: Ramp up = hochfahren; das Gegenteil ist ramp down.

items.def: extremely important because other things depend on it
items.ex: Her report played a pivotal role in the final decision.

items.def: existing as a natural and permanent part of something
items.ex: Some risk is inherent in every new project.

items.def: reasonable and likely to be true
items.ex: His explanation sounded plausible, but we still checked the numbers.

items.def: so convincing that you feel you must accept it
items.ex: She presented a compelling argument for changing suppliers.

items.def: showing small but important differences
items.ex: We need a more nuanced view of customer satisfaction.

items.def: logical and well organized so that it is easy to follow
items.ex: The report offers a coherent plan for the next quarter.

items.def: to make a bad situation worse
items.ex: Cutting the support team would only exacerbate the problem.

items.def: to make a problem or pain less severe
items.ex: Hiring temporary staff should alleviate the pressure on the team.

items.def: to make it harder for something to happen
items.ex: Unclear requirements hinder the progress of the whole project.

items.def: to start a task and accept responsibility for it
items.ex: The agency will undertake a full review of our security.

items.def: to state that something is true, especially in a debate
items.ex: The lawyers contend that the contract was never valid.

items.def: to publicly support a plan or idea
items.ex: Several managers advocate a four-day week for the whole company.

items.def: to reduce or limit something
items.ex: The company had to curtail its travel budget this year.

items.def: to examine something very carefully
items.ex: Auditors will scrutinize every transaction from the last quarter.

items.def: to support or form the basis of something
items.ex: Strong customer relationships underpin our long-term growth in the European market.

items.def: to collect information and put it together in a list or report
items.ex: She compiled a report from data supplied by five departments.

items.def: to become smaller or make something smaller
items.ex: Frequent delays diminish the trust of our customers.

items.def: existing commonly at a particular time or place
items.ex: Remote work is now prevalent in the software industry.

items.def: certain to happen and impossible to avoid
items.ex: Some delays were inevitable given the size of the project.

items.def: never having happened before
items.ex: The company faced an unprecedented increase in orders.

items.def: strict and very carefully controlled
items.ex: Banks must meet stringent requirements for data protection.

items.def: likely to change suddenly and unpredictably
items.ex: Oil prices have been highly volatile this year.

items.def: producing a lot of money
items.ex: The contract turned out to be far more lucrative than expected.

items.def: necessary as a basic part of a whole
items.ex: Customer feedback is integral to our product development.

items.def: a complicated and often unwelcome result of an action
items.ex: We must consider the legal ramifications of this decision.

items.def: something that encourages people to do something
items.ex: A small bonus is a strong incentive for the sales team.

items.def: a problem that must be solved before you can continue
items.ex: The biggest hurdle is getting approval from the regulator.

items.def: a hidden danger or difficulty
items.ex: One common pitfall is underestimating the training time.

items.def: the range of things that a project or activity includes
items.ex: The scope of the audit was extended to all subsidiaries.

items.def: a problem that delays or reverses progress
items.ex: The failed test was a serious setback for the project.

items.def: after something else has happened
items.ex: The company was subsequently acquired by a larger competitor.

items.def: in a way that is a basic part of something
items.ex: Long-term forecasts are inherently uncertain, especially in a volatile market.

items.def: in the end, after everything has been considered
items.ex: Ultimately, the decision rests with the managing director.

items.def: by a very small amount
items.ex: Revenue rose only marginally compared with last year.

items.def: growing larger by one addition after another
items.ex: The cumulative effect of small delays was significant.

items.def: to give more detail about something
items.ex: Could you elaborate on the risks you mentioned earlier?

items.def: able to recover quickly from difficulties
items.ex: Small suppliers are often more resilient than we expect.

items.def: a person or group with an interest in a project
items.ex: Every key stakeholder must approve the plan before we start.

items.def: the gradual growth of a project beyond its original goals
items.ex: Scope creep doubled the workload within three months.

items.def: an important point or event in a project
items.ex: We reached the first milestone two weeks ahead of schedule.

items.def: the number of people employed by a company
items.ex: The board approved an increase in headcount for next year.

items.def: a source of income for a business
items.ex: Subscriptions are our most reliable revenue stream, even in a weak quarter.

items.def: the difference between income and costs, as a percentage
items.ex: The profit margin on this product is only eight percent.

items.def: the movement of money into and out of a business
items.ex: Late payments are causing serious cash flow problems.

items.def: a careful check of a company before a deal
items.ex: The buyer completed due diligence in less than six weeks.

items.def: a measure that shows how well a goal is being achieved
items.ex: Customer retention is our most important key performance indicator.

items.def: the process of helping new employees or users get started
items.ex: A good onboarding program reduces the number of early resignations.

items.def: a system that lets users log in once for several applications
items.ex: Single sign-on saves staff from remembering many passwords.

items.def: a security method that needs two forms of proof of identity
items.ex: We now require two-factor authentication for all remote access.

items.def: an event in which private information is seen by unauthorized people
items.ex: The company reported a data breach to the authorities within a day.

items.def: a security system that blocks unauthorized network access
items.ex: The firewall blocked several suspicious connection attempts overnight.

items.def: the ability of a system to handle growth
items.ex: Scalability was the main reason we chose this platform.

items.def: a plan that shows future goals and steps
items.ex: The product roadmap includes three major releases next year.

items.def: a pile of work that has not been done yet
items.ex: We have a backlog of about two hundred support tickets.

items.def: a document that lists the risks of a project
items.ex: Please add the supplier delay to the risk register.

items.def: a method for finding the main reason for a problem
items.ex: A root cause analysis showed that the error began during data entry.

items.def: the rules that apply to a contract or service
items.ex: Please read the terms and conditions before you sign.

items.def: a contract that forbids sharing confidential information
items.ex: Both parties signed a non-disclosure agreement before the first meeting.

items.def: an official document that tells a supplier what to deliver
items.ex: The purchase order must be approved by the finance department.

items.def: the network of companies that produce and deliver a product
items.ex: Our supply chain was disrupted by the port strike.

items.def: the time between placing an order and receiving it
items.ex: The lead time for custom parts is about twelve weeks.

items.def: money that customers owe to a company
items.ex: Accounts receivable increased by ten percent last quarter.

items.def: a statement of what a company owns and owes
items.ex: The balance sheet shows a healthy level of cash.

items.def: an unexpected event that prevents a contract from being fulfilled
items.ex: The storm was declared an event of force majeure.

items.def: spreading work evenly across several servers
items.ex: Load balancing keeps the website fast during busy periods.

items.def: a connection between two software systems using an API
items.ex: The API integration lets the shop update stock levels automatically.

items.def: moving data and applications to cloud servers
items.ex: The cloud migration will be completed over the weekend.

items.def: an authorized attack on a system to find security weaknesses
items.ex: An external firm carried out a penetration test in March.

items.def: a team that helps users with technical problems
items.ex: Please contact the service desk if you cannot log in.

items.def: a formal proposal to change part of a project
items.ex: Every change request must be approved by the steering group.

items.def: the introduction of new ideas or methods (verb: innovate, adjective: innovative)
items.ex: Our biggest innovation this year is a faster checkout process.
items.why: Betonung auf der ersten Silbe: INnovation; dazu das Verb innovate und das Adjektiv innovative.

items.def: a careful study of something (verb: analyze, adjective: analytical)
items.ex: The analysis shows that costs rose in every region.
items.why: Der Plural ist analyses, nicht analysises; US-Verb analyze, nicht analyse.

items.def: the state of needing something (verb: depend, adjective: dependent)
items.ex: Our dependence on one supplier is a serious risk.
items.why: Das Nomen endet auf -ence, das Adjektiv ist dependent; dependable heißt „zuverlässig“.

items.def: something you accept as true without proof (verb: assume)
items.ex: The forecast rests on the assumption that prices stay stable.
items.why: Assumption heißt „Annahme“, nicht „Übernahme“; Verb assume.

items.def: a promise or strong dedication (verb: commit)
items.ex: We value the commitment of our long-serving employees.
items.why: Verb commit wird zu committed (t verdoppelt), aber commitment hat nur ein t und zwei m.

items.def: the ability to do something well (adjective: competent)
items.ex: Her competence in negotiation impressed the whole board.
items.why: Das Nomen hat -ence, das Adjektiv competent hat -ent; nicht „competition“ verwechseln.

items.def: a change made to suit new conditions (verb: adapt, adjective: adaptable)
items.ex: The adaptation of the product for the US market took a year.
items.why: Adapt (anpassen) und adopt (übernehmen) unterscheiden sich nur durch einen Buchstaben.

items.def: the act of making someone agree (verb: persuade, adjective: persuasive)
items.ex: It took a lot of persuasion to get the board on our side.
